title: Is GPT-4 Less Politically Biased than GPT-3.5? A Renewed Investigation of ChatGPT’s Political Biases
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT exhibits political bias and personality-like response patterns, and whether GPT-4 is less politically biased than GPT-3.5. The authors focus on three questions: whether the models show political biases and personality traits, whether those biases differ between GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, and whether the relationships between political orientation and personality traits in the models resemble correlations reported in human research.

The study does not involve students, teachers, or any educational intervention. Instead, the authors repeatedly administer two questionnaires directly to the language models through the OpenAI API: the Political Compass Test and a 50-item Big Five Personality Test. Each model (gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 and gpt-4-0314) completed the tests 100 times under default and role-assigned conditions (e.g., libertarian-left, authoritarian-right). The analysis includes averages, standard deviations, Brunner-Munzel significance tests comparing the two models, and correlations between political-compass scores and Big Five trait scores, including an examination of test-order effects.

The context is an online API-based evaluation of LLM outputs rather than a human-participant study. No educational population is sampled, and no writing, feedback, revision, or classroom implementation is studied. The main findings are that both GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 show libertarian-left tendencies on the Political Compass; GPT-4 appears only negligibly less biased than GPT-3.5; GPT-4 is better at emulating assigned political roles; both models show pronounced Openness and Agreeableness, with GPT-4 showing higher Neuroticism; and some correlations between political orientation and personality traits resemble patterns found in human studies. The paper concludes that political bias remains present in both models and that sequencing effects suggest a form of contextual carryover across prompts.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is not an education intervention study and does not evaluate formative feedback on student-authored drafts. It is an arXiv methodological study of political bias and personality traits in GPT-3.5 versus GPT-4 using repeated questionnaire administrations to the models themselves, with no student sample, no grades 9-12 population, no writing task, no comparator relevant to educational feedback, and no educational outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports no direct educational impact on student writing, literacy, revision quality, or classroom outcomes. Therefore it provides no usable evidence of impact for the target K-12 LLM feedback intervention question.
